human_tolerance.notes: Prefers 'open habitats with clumps of trees' and lives in meadows, farmlands and suburbs, foraging around feedlots, grain elevators, landfills, barns and houses. 'Where persecuted it becomes very wary, but otherwise it is fairly tolerant of human presence.' light_max and flight_distance_m are judgement, not separately sourced numbers.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Nest building by both sexes over 40-50 days, starting in February (later in the northern part of the range); a domed twig nest near the top of a tree.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding runs from late March to early July. Clutches average six or seven eggs (up to thirteen); incubation 16-21 days by the female alone; nestling period three to four weeks; young fly 3-4 weeks after hatching and feed with adults for about two months.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Pairs form in the first or second year and often hold the same nest tree across successive seasons; only the nest tree and its immediate surroundings are defended, so nests may clump into a diffuse colony where trees are scarce.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Non-breeding and juvenile birds associate in loose groups, typically around open feeding sites such as feedlots, grain elevators and landfills.

vocalizations.description: The species' most common call: an alarm chatter described as 'ka-ka-ka-ka', sometimes preceded with 'skah-skah'. It is very different from the Eurasian magpie's chatter and is also used as the contact call from a perch.

The softer cooing call from the wider repertoire, which Wikipedia describes as a mix of tweets, coos, purrs, shrills and squawks. At least one magpie living with humans has learned to imitate human speech.

external.note: GBIF usage key and authorship read from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy; the iNaturalist taxon id (143853) matched the accepted name 'Black-billed Magpie' in the iNaturalist taxa API; ITIS TSN and NCBI taxon id from Wikidata (P815, P685), cross-checked against ITIS.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern; Wikipedia: 'Today, they are considered a species of least concern by the IUCN'.

range.note: Country and state list derived from the Distribution and habitat section: 'ranges from coastal southern Alaska, southwest Yukon Territory, central British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and northwestern Ontario in the north, through the Rocky Mountains down south to all the Rocky Mountain states including New Mexico, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and some bordering states', with casual records as far east as northern Minnesota and Iowa. An approximation of the range, not an exhaustive one; the species is absent in California west of the Cascades and Sierra Nevada, where the yellow-billed magpie replaces it, so no Californian counties are implied by the country entry. elevation_m (0-3000 m) is judgement: the source describes the species from sea level in coastal Alaska south through the Rocky Mountains and does not give figures.

traits.note: Covers the structural traits (body plan, limb count, thermoregulation, skin, flight, respiration, metamorphosis, perching) and locomotion modes, which are read off the taxonomic placement, the class's physiology and the description of walking, hopping and following large predators on the wing. Individual numeric and behavioural traits below carry their own entries.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement mapping: the source describes 'domed nests which are made up of twigs and are located near the top of trees'; the schema's enum (Cup/Cavity/Platform/Ground/Burrow/None) has no domed-stick-nest option, so 'Platform' was chosen as the closest fit, the same mapping used for Pica pica.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (~0.18 kg); the validator's size-class bands place this in the Small band despite the magpie's long tail making it look larger.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of the male range midpoint (167-216 g -> 191.5 g) and the female range midpoint (141-179 g -> 160 g) = 175.8 g, rounded to 0.176 kg. The source notes males are on average 6-9% larger and 16-24% heavier than females.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Full span across sexes: females 141-179 g, males 167-216 g.

traits.wingspan_m.note: No sourced wingspan figure was found, and the Fly locomotion mode requires the field. Derived from the stated wing chords (males 205-219 mm, females 175-210 mm; overall midpoint 197 mm) at roughly 2.1x, the chord-to-span ratio typical of large corvids; 0.42 m. This is a conversion, not a measured value.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The source is inconsistent: the lead says 'black-billed magpies in the wild have a lifespan of six to seven years' while the breeding section says 'the lifespan of the species in the wild is about four to six years'. The midpoint of the lead's six to seven years was taken; the discrepancy is recorded here rather than silently resolved.

traits.diet.note: Judgement: no sourced percentages were found. The Feeding section lists the diet qualitatively - 'carrion, insects, seeds, berries, and nuts', plus garbage and pet or livestock food near humans, and hunting 'rodents, reptiles, amphibians, small birds' and other birds' eggs - and notes the species feeds 'primarily on animal matter during the summer' and switches 'to more vegetation' in winter. Shares follow that ordering, with invertebrates and fruit/seed the largest components.

traits.social.note: 'Adult black-billed magpie typically form pairs which last year-round and often for life', with a low divorce rate in one South Dakota study (8%). Non-breeders associate loosely, but the breeding social unit is a pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: a diurnal corvid, not explicitly labelled but consistent with the daytime foraging, nest building and nest defence described throughout the source.

traits.defense.note: 'If regularly disturbed, black-billed magpie pairs will aggressively defend their nest', and 'biologists who have climbed nest trees to measure magpie eggs have reported that the parents recognized them personally on subsequent days and started to mob them, overlooking other people in the vicinity' - hence Mob rather than Flee.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 'Where persecuted it becomes very wary, but otherwise it is fairly tolerant of human presence' - a middling value, above the confiding garden songbirds and below the species' wariness under persecution.

habitat.note: Covers shelter_tag and habitat.resources. Prey, carrion, fruit, seed and mast tags come from the Feeding section; nest_platform and perch tags from the Breeding and nesting section (nests near the top of trees) and the wide-ranging foraging behaviour. Weights are judgement, not separately sourced percentages.

habitat.use.note: Judgement split: the source says the species 'prefers generally open habitats with clumps of trees' and 'can also commonly be found in farmlands and suburban areas', nests near the top of trees, and 'also walks or hops on the ground, where it obtains food items such as beetles, grasshoppers, worms, and small rodents'. Roughly even, with a slight ground emphasis on foraging.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Distribution and habitat and lead sections: prefers open habitats with clumps of trees, common in farmlands and suburban areas, found around feedlots, grain elevators, landfills, barns and houses outside the breeding season, and fairly tolerant of people unless persecuted. flight_distance_m and light_max are judgement, not separately sourced numbers.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Black-billed magpies are generally non-migratory, however some winter movement does occur', thought to be postbreeding dispersal and return to nesting sites, so ActiveYearRound was used rather than Migration or PartialMigration.

seasonal.phases.note: Nest building over 40-50 days from February, breeding from late March to early July with clutch, incubation and nestling figures, year-round pair territoriality around the nest tree, and loose winter association at open feeding sites. Exact day-of-month boundaries other than the quoted 'late March'/'early July' are judgement; the breeding phase is tagged US-CO because the locale that prompted this record is in Colorado, and the source's dates are continental.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg (greenish grey with brown markings, 33 mm), altricial juvenile (hatched asynchronously, brooded by the female and fed by both sexes, flying 3-4 weeks after hatching and feeding with adults for about two months) and adult; no sourced juvenile-plumage duration was found, so duration_days is unset and the juvenile scale (0.85) is judgement reflecting a fledged young bird.

vocalizations.chatter.note: 'The most common is an alarm call, called a chatter, that is described as a ka-ka-ka-ka, sometimes preceded with skah-skah', and 'very different from that of the Eurasian magpie'.

vocalizations.coo.note: 'The vocalizations of the black-billed magpie consist of a number of calls variously described as tweets, coos, purrs, shrills and squawks'; the softer coo is taken as the contact call. Loudness and cooldown are judgement.

look.note: Description section: 'largely black, with white scapulars, belly, and primaries, and the wings and tail are an iridescent blue-green'; the tail is made of long layered feathers with the middle pair extending further, the beak is uniformly black and the irises black. The palette approximates the blue-green iridescence with a dark teal 'markings' colour on the tail and outer wing feathers, since the schema palette has no separate iridescent slot; proportions (long tail, medium build) are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: flee_m and wariness reflect a wary corvid that is fairly tolerant of people; food_tag is the largest seasonal diet component, matching the program default's insect foraging; song and alarm both point at the single chatter call, which the shared program requires and which the source gives no separate song for.
